text:
Tell me, mysterious light,
that wanders before my eyes,
awakens my interest
and charms my sleepless hours:

Are you perhaps a lamp
cast down from heaven,
passing as a pilgrim
through this wretched earth?

Are you a spirit or sylph
of our unspoiled homeland,
holding the fiery sap
of its young life within you?

Are you perhaps the wandering soul
of someone dear,
come to ask me for
remembrance and prayers;

or else a shining spark
from the bright wings
with which heavenly hope
sustains the sorrowful?

I do not know; but when you shine
beautifully before my eyes
in the solemn stillness
of tropical nights,

whether, a wandering exhalation,
you cross the clear sphere,
or play like a breeze,
swaying among the reeds;

whether, like a pure diamond,
you set yourself among the palms,
imitating their whisper,
adorning their green with light;

I seem to feel
a strange revelation
of mystical love
between your glow and my soul.

I seem to sense
secret harmonies
between the longing I conceal
and the radiance you give off.

O star or sylph,
soul or spirit, then,
cast brighter sparks
as my voice sings to you!

May the notes of my lyre
and the sparks of your flame
mingle and travel
through mountains and savannas,

and rise to heaven
in the fragrance of the fields,
where kindred stars
call them to themselves,

where he sets his throne
who understands and weighs
the essence of every light,
the cause of every longing!

translation.title: To a Firefly
